back: Given intranasally; noted side effects include liver toxicity and an association with breast cancer risk (with prolonged use).

subject: Endocrinology
front: What is the mechanism and clinical use of Cinacalcet?
back: It is a Calcium-Sensing Receptor (CaSR) agonist (calcimimetic) that mimics high calcium, thereby decreasing PTH secretion; used in the treatment of Hyperparathyroidism.

subject: Endocrinology
front: What are Teriparatide and Abaloparatide, and what is their mechanism?
back: Shortened (35 amino acid) fragments of PTH (PTH 1-34) that stimulate osteoblasts.

subject: Endocrinology
front: What is the maximum recommended duration of use for PTH analogues (Teriparatide/Abaloparatide), and why?
back: Maximum 2 years, due to an increased risk of osteosarcoma with prolonged use.

subject: Endocrinology
front: What is Romosozumab, and what is its dual mechanism of action?
back: A dual-action osteoporosis drug that increases osteoblast activity while decreasing sclerostin (a sclerostin inhibitor with both anabolic and antiresorptive effects).

subject: Endocrinology
front: What is Strontium's classification in osteoporosis treatment?
back: It is classified as a dual-action agent (both stimulates osteoblasts and inhibits osteoclasts).

subject: Endocrinology
front: What is the intracellular signaling cascade downstream of receptor tyrosine kinases (the MAP kinase pathway)?
back: Ligand binding activates the receptor tyrosine kinase, which recruits the Ras-Sos-Grb2 complex; this activates Raf-1, which activates MAPKK, which activates MAPK - leading to downstream changes in gene transcription.

subject: Endocrinology
deck: Part-5: Pituitary - Hypothalamic Axis & Anterior Pituitary
front: Why does renal failure cause secondary hyperprolactinemia?
back: Renal insufficiency decreases the renal excretion/clearance of prolactin, causing it to accumulate in the blood.

subject: Endocrinology
front: How does serum sodium differ across SIADH, Central DI, Nephrogenic DI, Primary Polydipsia, and Diabetes Mellitus?
back: SIADH: decreased (hyponatremia, euvolemic); Central DI: increased; Nephrogenic DI: increased; Primary Polydipsia: normal/decreased; Diabetes Mellitus: no significant change (unless severe osmotic diuresis occurs).

subject: Endocrinology
front: What classic hand/finger sign is associated with Pseudohypoparathyroidism (Albright Hereditary Osteodystrophy)?
back: Shortening of the 4th (and often 5th) metacarpal, producing a visible "dimple" sign when a fist is made (knuckle-knuckle-dimple-dimple sign).

subject: Endocrinology
front: Besides diabetes-specific autoantibodies, what else is Type 1 DM associated with?
back: Association with other autoimmune conditions (e.g., autoimmune thyroid disease, celiac disease, Addison's disease, vitiligo).

subject: Endocrinology
front: How are the four main diabetes types organized by age category and habitus in the classification tree?
back: Young: Lean habitus = Type 1 DM; Lean/normal habitus = MODY. Adults: Obese habitus = Type 2 DM; Lean/normal habitus = LADA.

subject: Endocrinology
front: Besides bisphosphonates, what other treatment can cause osteonecrosis of the jaw, and which bone is most commonly affected?
back: Radiotherapy (RT) can also cause osteonecrosis of the jaw; the mandible is the bone most commonly affected.

subject: Endocrinology
deck: Part-5: Pituitary - Hypothalamic Axis & Anterior Pituitary
front: Besides prostate cancer, what other hormone-sensitive cancer can continuous GnRH agonist therapy be used for?
back: Hormone receptor-positive breast cancer in premenopausal women (via ovarian suppression) - noted in BTR notes alongside prostate cancer.

subject: Endocrinology
front: Besides decreasing insulin secretion (causing hyperglycemia), what other metabolic side effect do thiazide diuretics have?
back: Thiazides also cause hyperuricemia (increased uric acid), in addition to decreasing insulin secretion.

subject: Endocrinology
front: By what mechanism does Primary Adrenal Insufficiency (Addison's disease) cause hyperpigmentation?
back: Loss of cortisol negative feedback increases pituitary POMC production; since ACTH and MSH are both derived from POMC (and ACTH itself has intrinsic MSH-like activity), the resulting high ACTH drives hyperpigmentation - the same POMC-based mechanism seen in Cushing Disease/Nelson Syndrome.

subject: Endocrinology
front: Besides TB, what other granulomatous infection is noted as a cause of Primary Adrenal Insufficiency?
back: Histoplasmosis (in addition to Tuberculosis and autoimmune destruction).

subject: Endocrinology
deck: Part-5: Pituitary - Hypothalamic Axis & Anterior Pituitary
front: What normal prolactin cutoff is noted in the BTR 2.0 notes, and how does it relate to the coreBTR screening range?
back: BTR 2.0 notes a normal PRL cutoff of <20 ng/mL (any value above is abnormal); coreBTR further specifies that a level of 40-200 ng/mL should prompt work-up for secondary causes before diagnosing a prolactinoma.
